newsitem.title: UK: Swedish crown rises as EMU entry in 1999 ruled out.
newsitem.headline: Swedish crown rises as EMU entry in 1999 ruled out.

text.p: The Swedish crown rose against the mark after Prime Minister Goran Persson said Sweden won't join the European single currency in 1999 but left the door open to a later entry.

"People were pretty much expecting this but decided to buy some (crowns) anyway given the moves into safe havens which aren't going to be in the first wave of EMU," said Craig Justham, the deputy manager of foreign exchange at Creditanstalt Bankverein.
Sweden's Persson said public opinion was too opposed to European economic and monetary, and the outlook for the project too uncertain for Sweden to join from the scheduled outset in 1999.
He also said a decision on whether to take Sweden into EMU will only be made after either a referendum or an election.
The statement, the first time the ruling Social Democrats have publicly stated their view on EMU, triggered demand for crowns as traders saw it as a safe haven from concern about a broad EMU.
Mark/Swedish crown fell to 4.48, matching the low it set on May 23. It was last at 4.4905/35 from 4.5115/45 in late Europe on Monday.

Speculation the single currency will be founded by a broad group of countries has grown after the French Socialists won power in elections Sunday. They are calling for Italy and Spain to be included in EMU from the outset.

The German government may find it difficult to keep these countries out of EMU from the start, given the trouble it is having reducing its own budget deficit to the 3 percent of gross domestic product required of EMU entrants. Its woes were highlighted on Tuesday after it was forced to back down from plans to revalue the Bundesbank's reserves in 1997.
"The question is how will Germany meet the 3 percent target," said Julian Jessop, an economist at Nikko Europe.
"A soft EMU, with Italy in at the start, is foremost in the market's minds at the moment," he added.
Ruled out of EMU entry from the outset, the crown should benefit from the safe haven flows which have bolstered the dollar, sterling, and the yen against the mark in the past week.
Ian Amstad, an economist at Bankers Trust, predicted such flows could help the crown to strengthen towards 4.30 per mark this summer if Swedish growth holds up and interest rates aren't cut further.
More immediately, Justham at Creditanstalt, is expecting the crown to move to 4.46 per mark.
